name: WARDEN — private browser
subtitle: No account. No telemetry.
promotionalText: A private entry point for people who run networks: no account, no analytics, no sensor access, and a posture screen that states only what is actually enforced.
description:
WARDEN is a private entry point to the web for security and network administrators. This is the mobile companion to WARDEN for Windows.

It opens on an address field and a short, honest statement of what the session does and does not do — no decorative shield, no badge claiming protections the app does not have.

WHAT IT DOES
• Opens any address or search in the system browser view, so a page never shares an origin, a script context or a session with the app's own interface.
• Keeps no browsing history, no profile and no identifiers of its own. The app cannot read the pages it opens.
• Ships no analytics, crash-reporting or advertising SDKs, and requests no camera, microphone or location access.
• Offers quick destinations to the project's repository, its release notes and the privacy policy.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO YET
• It does not block ads or trackers, and it does not encrypt DNS. Request-level blocking, per-tab isolation and DNS over HTTPS are the next phase, planned in the public repository; the app itself says so rather than implying otherwise.
• There is no account, no purchase, no subscription and nothing to configure before the first page loads.

WHO IT IS FOR
Administrators who want a small, auditable starting point on a phone that asks for no permissions and phones home to nobody.

PRIVACY
Data collected: none. Full policy: https://innotelinc.github.io/warden/privacy.html

answers.Unrestricted Web Access: Yes — the address field opens any public URL. This is the capability that sets the rating; Chrome, Firefox and DuckDuckGo are all rated 16+ for the same reason.
answers.Violence, Profanity, Horror, Medical, Al: None — the app ships no content of its own beyond its own interface text.
answers.In-App Controls: None claimed. The app has no content of its own to gate.

ageRating.note: App Store Connect now uses 4+/9+/13+/16+/18+, and the questionnaire requires answers for new submissions. Answering 'Unrestricted Web Access' honestly is what produces 16+; do not answer 4+ to make the listing look friendlier.

reviewNotes:
WARDEN is a browser entry point for security and network administrators, and the mobile companion to an existing desktop product whose source is public at https://github.com/innotelinc/warden. No sign-in, demo account or purchase is required, and no permission prompt appears at any point.

HOW TO TEST
1. Launch the app. The first screen is an address field and a 'Session posture' list that states in plain language what the app does and does not do.
2. Type a host such as example.com and press return, or tap a Quick destination. The page opens full screen in a system browser view (SFSafariViewController).
3. Dismiss that view to return to the app. The camera, microphone, location, contacts and tracking permissions are never requested.

WHY THIS IS NOT A WRAPPER AROUND ONE WEBSITE
The app bundles no site, runs no server of its own and has no account, so there is no website being repackaged. The interface is the product: address resolution (bare host, IP address or search term), the posture screen, and the quick destinations. Pages are deliberately handed to the system browser view instead of an in-app web view, so a page can never see or script the app's interface.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT
Request-level ad and tracker blocking, per-tab isolation and DNS over HTTPS are on the public roadmap and are not in this build. The app says that on its own first screen, and the description says it too, rather than implying protections it does not have.

AGE RATING
'Unrestricted Web Access' is answered Yes, because the address field opens any public URL. That answer is what sets the rating to 16+.

EXPORT COMPLIANCE
ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption is false in Info.plist: the app uses only the HTTPS provided by the operating system and implements no cryptography of its own. App/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy declares no tracking and no collected data, and no required-reason API beyond the two Capacitor's bridge touches (UserDefaults and file timestamps).
